summary: Weak keyword co-occurrence in utility module; no traced installer harm
details: The package's lib/Utils/generics.js triggered a keyword co-occurrence match on the tokens 'ping', 'GET', and 'id' spread across widely separated lines. This is the typical shape of a utilities module (HTTP helper GETs, an ID generator, and a 'ping' identifier or timeout keepalive) rather than a targeted exfiltration primitive. No hardcoded attacker C2 endpoint, credential-path read (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser stores), env-var scraping, install-time fetch-and-execute, dropper, or lifecycle hook was identified. Without corroborating evidence tying a specific installer-side data read to a specific non-first-party destination, the pattern alone does not demonstrate attacker benefit against the installer. A human reviewer should confirm the semantic role of the flagged lines before publishing a verdict.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
